intent: Build a Slack bot that summarizes daily standup threads and posts a digest each morning.

models.name: Qwen3 4B Instruct (4-bit, on-device)
models.cost_basis_note: Operator's own hardware, not a vendor rate: a $3,000 machine over a 10,000-hour life ($0.30/hr) plus 40W at $0.20/kWh ($0.008/hr), divided by measured throughput on that machine (~430 tok/s prompt, ~60 tok/s generation). Charging power alone, on the argument the machine was bought anyway, would put generation at ~$0.04/1M instead; both bases are defensible and a $0 rate is not. Context/output ceilings left null pending the model card for the exact build in use.

blueprint_rows.name: Parse and summarize each standup thread
blueprint_rows.description: Read a day's standup thread per channel and produce a short structured summary.

effectiveness.reason: A wrong summary costs a human a re-read of the thread, moderate but not severe cost of error.

efficiency.reason: Runs once per channel per day, low volume, no human watching latency.

difficulty.reason: Bounded summarization over well-specified input/output, not open-ended reasoning.

pick.what_flips_it: If daily volume exceeds ~50 channels, drop to Haiku on a batch call to hold latency/cost.
pick.why_not_tier_above: Opus's extra reasoning depth isn't needed for a bounded single-thread summary.
pick.why_not_tier_below: Haiku's smaller context risks truncating a long thread before it's summarized.

blueprint_rows.rationale: Bounded, well-specified summarization; Sonnet at low effort clears the bar for a fraction of the default tier's cost.

blueprint_rows.name: Look up each channel's configured digest recipients
blueprint_rows.description: Resolve which users should receive a given channel's digest.
blueprint_rows.query_layer_note: Answered by a single indexed lookup against the workspace's channel-config table; route via a deterministic query layer instead of a model call.

effectiveness.reason: A wrong lookup just misroutes one message; cheap to catch and retry.

efficiency.reason: Runs once per channel per day, pure key-value lookup, no reasoning content.

difficulty.reason: Single indexed lookup against structured config, no ambiguity.

pick.what_flips_it: If recipient routing ever needs interpreting free-text preferences instead of a structured config row, promote to a model call.

blueprint_rows.rationale: Pure structured lookup; a query layer is reliable by construction and removes hallucination risk entirely, at less cost than even the cheapest model tier.

blueprint_rows.name: Pre-filter the day's threads for ones that mention a blocker
blueprint_rows.description: Sweep every thread in the day's backlog and shortlist the ones the summarization stage should read closely. Recall-tuned: the summarizer still re-reads every hit, so this stage never produces a claim anyone acts on directly.

effectiveness.reason: A false positive costs one extra read downstream and a false negative is caught by the summarizer, so cost of error is low and bounded.

efficiency.reason: Highest-volume stage in the flow, every thread in every channel daily, and nothing interactive waits on it.

difficulty.reason: One fuzzy yes/no per thread against a single well-specified signal, no cross-thread reasoning.

pick.what_flips_it: If the shortlist ever becomes the deliverable instead of an input the summarizer re-reads, or if the stage has to run where no local runtime is installed, it goes to Haiku: a local pick is barred from producing output anyone reads directly, and it must never be the only path.
pick.why_not_tier_above: Sonnet's reasoning depth buys nothing on a one-signal recall-tuned filter whose misses are caught one stage later.
pick.why_not_tier_below: The only tier below is a keyword grep, which cannot catch the paraphrases ('stuck on', 'waiting on review') this filter exists for.

blueprint_rows.rationale: Bulk, mechanical, off the critical path, and unverified output a stronger stage re-reads: the routing gate's deny and compound checks both pass, and the amortized local basis undercuts Haiku at this volume. Falls back to the Haiku runner-up wherever no local runtime is present.

pick.what_flips_it: If daily volume exceeds ~50 channels, drop to Haiku on a batch call to hold latency/cost.

work_routing_map.rationale: Same reasoning as stage-1: bounded summarization, Sonnet at low effort.

fields.name: matched
fields.description: Whether the thread mentions a blocker.

fields.name: quote
fields.description: The verbatim span the match came from; a match with no quote is dropped rather than passed on.

fields.name: unverified
fields.description: Always true on this seam: the producing tier is a local model, so the consumer treats every field as a candidate, not a fact.

exclude: the local model's own reasoning about why it matched
any judgment about whether the blocker is real or already resolved

assumptions: A channel-config table already exists and is queryable
would_measure: Actual per-channel summary token count once real thread lengths are known
Whether Haiku alone clears the bar once volume passes the stated flip condition

calibration.notes: No recommended-vs-actual calibration history available yet for this repo; reasoned from first principles.
